title: cross-sdk-session-cache-adapter-and-pauseable-stream-ergonomics-bump
author: Asha Fernandez
release_notes: Introduce a lightweight session cache adapter and pause/resume helpers for streaming clients. Bumps Python/TS/Go SDKs for parity and ergonomic defaults. No breaking API surface for existing call patterns.
description: Context: Multiple product teams reported inconsistent session token caching behavior and mismatched streaming ergonomics across our three official SDKs. This caused duplicate handshake traffic and awkward client code for pause/resume. Motivation: provide a small, well-documented adapter that centralizes short-lived session caching and a cross-sdk pauseable stream helper so customers can implement backpressure and client-side pause/resume without bespoke code. This PR contains: - a runtime-agnostic SessionCacheAdapter interface used by SDKs to store ephemeral session leases and to expose a single refresh path - pause/resume helpers for streaming consumers (Python/TS/Go) with the same public method names and semantics (pause(), resume(), on_paused) - minor ergonomic sugar: default retry profile for auth refresh, and a new client option `session_cache` that accepts either adapter or a simple factory - version bumps for SDK packages (python -> 0.12.1, typescript -> 1.7.0, go -> 0.10.0) - docs and examples under /docs/sdk-session-cache and three small integration tests per SDK Checklist: - [x] design RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2248/session-cache-adapter (linked) - [x] unit tests for adapter and helpers - [x] integration smoke tests (CI) - [x] docs and migration guide - [x] reviewers signoff Notes: There are no breaking changes for users who don't opt into the new session_cache option; default behavior remains the same. The adapter adds a single opt-in extension point for large deployments who want to centralize session leasing and reduce handshake noise.
